overview: Otoh Gunga is a underwater city on Naboo, documented across Films · Clone Wars. Otoh Gunga is the Gungan bubble-city beneath Naboo's swamps, seat of Boss Nass and launching point for the Grand Army's shielded counterattack.
history:
Otoh Gunga began as a underwater city anchor on Naboo, positioned where water, ore, hyperspace lanes, or sacred geography forced travelers to stop. Otoh Gunga grew where Naboo's resources—water, ore, kyber, or trade lanes—forced travelers to stop, creating a underwater city that outlasted first founders. Early survey maps from the Old Republic era list Otoh Gunga as a mandatory customs point for sector governors and Jedi exploration teams. Films, Clone Wars, Rebels, Mandalorian, Ahsoka, KOTOR, KOTOR II, TOR, and Sith Empire narratives all treat Otoh Gunga as more than scenery—it is a decision point.

Ancient and pre-Republic layers beneath Otoh Gunga include buried fortresses, Rakatan relics, and Sith ward-stones that still disrupt modern sensors. Pre-Republic and Sith-era layers beneath Otoh Gunga include ward-stones, Rakatan markers, and Massassi masonry that modern engineers still discover during repaving. Local archives recovered from Naboo suggest Otoh Gunga once governed trade policy for entire subsectors before centralization on Coruscant.

In the modern era, Otoh Gunga expanded through prefab districts, orbital elevators, and refugee camps that fused multiple species into a single urban rhythm. Clone Wars, Imperial occupation, and New Republic rebuilding each added districts to Otoh Gunga; Mandalorian and Ahsoka-era storylines treat it as a live operational hub. Mandalorian-era bounties and Ahsoka-era investigations repeatedly lead back to Otoh Gunga because its ports lack the scrutiny of Core World bureaucracy. New Republic planners studied Otoh Gunga as a template for rebuilding settlements after the Imperial collapse, citing both its failures and its innovations.

Otoh Gunga has been invaded, liberated, blockaded, and rebuilt more times than most planetary capitals, making its streets a palimpsest of battle damage. Battle dossiers from KOTOR sieges, TOR planetary incursions, and Galactic Civil War raids mark Otoh Gunga as strategically contested on Naboo. Clone Wars dossiers mark Otoh Gunga as strategically vital; Imperial Era governors exploited that same geography to punish rebellious populations. KOTOR-era records and TOR-era campaign logs show earlier iterations of the same struggle—control of Otoh Gunga meant control of Naboo.
significance:
The economy of Otoh Gunga runs on layered industries: docking fees, black-market mediation, sacred tourism, factory output, or casino finance depending on the era. Otoh Gunga's economy mixes legal trade with shadow finance—dock fees, kolto or tibanna exports, scavenging, or casino revenue depending on era and governor. Cultural life in Otoh Gunga mixes planetary tradition with imported habits from every species that ever missed a connection and stayed. Markets, cantinas, and temples in Otoh Gunga blend Naboo native ritual with offworld imports, producing music and cuisine that signal rebel safe houses to trained eyes. Music, food, and festival calendars in Otoh Gunga are used by rebels to signal safe houses and by Imperials to track dissident networks. Otoh Gunga influences galactic history disproportionately because leaders, smugglers, and prophets treat it as neutral ground until it suddenly is not. Treaties, betrayals, and superweapon strikes linked to Otoh Gunga altered fleet movements across the Old Republic through Sequel Era conflicts. Scenes set in Otoh Gunga across the saga often mark turning points: treaties signed, betrayals exposed, or the first shot of a regional war. Settlement planners across the Rim still cite Otoh Gunga when arguing for open ports versus fortified capitals—a debate renewed after every occupation.
